A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROSE study and provide complete, readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The relocated appendix material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original mathematical-reasoning experiments with Qwen and Llama models, including benchmark results, ablations, response-length analyses, and case studies in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results. Response-length and exploration analyses appear in Sections 5.6–5.7, while the case studies remain in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same semantic-entropy branching, epsilon-exploration, segment-level advantage estimation, length-aware calibration, and training objective. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on 7,500 MATH problems and evaluate AIME2024, AIME2025, AMC23, and MATH500. Newly cited benchmarks and domains are not added to the experiments.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the base-model, GRPO, DAPO, Dr.GRPO, TreePO, and FR3E comparisons. Comparator membership also remains unchanged in the branching, efficiency, and ablation experiments.

E3.justification: The three model backbones, training budgets, preprocessing, decoding settings, and pass@8 evaluation with eight responses per question remain unchanged. Table 1 retains the same best-score-during-training reporting rule.

E4.justification: The branching-metric comparisons, diversity analysis, length-calibration sweep, component ablations, epsilon sweep, and case studies are all retained. V1 Appendices A.1–A.2 become v2 Sections 5.6–5.7 without new analyses.

E5.justification: Point-score reporting and Figure 4's similarity-distribution statistics are unchanged. Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the plotted and case-study results remain unchanged after matching relocated material. For example, Table 1 retains ROSE average pass@8 scores of 51.24, 55.75, and 31.67 for Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Llama-3.2-3B, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), including the entropy definitions, node values, advantage estimates, length calibration, and optimization objective, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or theoretical results are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about exploration diversity, reasoning accuracy, and efficiency. Moving supporting analyses into the main text does not change their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning local exploration, reasoning diversity, length–accuracy tradeoffs, and case-study errors are retained. The limitations concerning mathematical tasks and models of at most 8B parameters are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same VeRL implementation, hyperparameters, token limits, embedding model, eight A800 GPUs, and code-access link. Relocating analyses adds no reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 adds AttnPO and several RLVR, exploration, and benchmark citations, while removing references to Kimi K1.5, Tulu 3, Light-R1, and MM-Eureka. These changes refresh the background bibliography without substantially revising ROSE's positioning or comparative discussion.

P1.justification: Appendices A.1–A.2 move to Sections 5.6–5.7, and Appendix A.3 becomes Appendix A. Author contact and corresponding-author information are added. Most prose is unchanged; two updated cross-references incorrectly retain the label 'Appendix' for the new main-text sections.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and Table 5 move from the appendix into the main text, and Figure 6 now appears on a separate page. The same five tables and seven figures retain their content and visual design, with localized changes to placement and pagination.

improvement.justification: V2 refreshes citations and makes existing analyses more prominent, but leaves the methods, evidence, explanations, and limitations unchanged. The modest presentation benefits are accompanied by incorrect 'Appendix 5.6' and 'Appendix 5.7' references. These limited editorial changes leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
